title: Les Demoiselles d'Avignon, Picasso
subject: art
description: Five nudes with facets and masks: Les Demoiselles d'Avignon breaks mimesis and opens up cubism. Scandal even among Picasso's friends.

hero.hook: The painting that Picasso kept turned against the wall… before he changed the art.

blocks.text: In **1907**, in Montmartre, **Picasso** completed *The Young Ladies of Avignon*. Five women, broken bodies, masked faces. The  is in the making. [[Cubism]]
Even those close to him are shocked. , the gentle imitation of reality, is dead. [[mimesis]]

Picasso works at , cites poor artists. The title refers to a street in Barcelona linked to prostitution. The nude is no longer the Greek ideal: it is frontal, disturbing. [[Le Bateau-Lavoir (Montmartre)]]
Dozens of studies precede the painting. Picasso hesitates, corrects, hardens. The result is not an improvisation: it is a calculated attack on taste.

blocks.caption: Five looks that no longer caress.

blocks.text: The faces on the right are inspired by African and Iberian . This is : looking for a force outside the European academic canon. [[arts premiers]] [[Primitivism in modern art]]
The two figures on the right, more masked, mark the break. We move from the Western nude to another logic of the face, more conceptual than carnal.
Picasso hesitated for a long time to show the painting, aware of its violence.
The facets announce the . Braque, initially stunned, soon joined Picasso in the deconstruction of space. [[analytical cubism]]
Remaining little shown for a long time, the painting nevertheless influenced Braque and the Cubist suite. Its violence needs time to become “classic”.

blocks.caption: From the ritual mask to the modern grid.

blocks.text: Today at MoMA, the work remains the “big bang” of 20th century art. Everything that fragments the visible owes it something.
To fully understand Les Demoiselles d'Avignon, Picasso, you must keep one thing in mind: each technical detail serves an emotion or an idea. The work is never just decorative.
Context matters as much as style. Dates, places, sponsors, public: all this explains why a form appears at a specific moment, and not before.
Finally, legacy is measured over the long term. What we see today in museums, films or popular music still bears the traces of these inventions.
At MoMA, it is today an obligatory stop. We sometimes forget that he was initially an object of scandal even for the avant-garde.
To fully understand Les Demoiselles d'Avignon, Picasso, you must keep one thing in mind: each technical detail serves an emotion or an idea. The work is never just decorative.
In 1907, Les Demoiselles d'Avignon broke the classical nude and opened the way to Cubism.
